summary: Adapter-chaining middleware creates extra synchronous round-trips causing end-to-end latency spikes and request timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic end-to-end latency spikes and downstream 504/502 timeouts when invoking sequences that call two or more external adapters (connectors) within a single request. Impact: Live production workloads for ScaleSky Labs experiencing ~10-30% request timeouts during peak traffic windows, resulting in failed transactions and user-visible errors. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated pool (dedicated-tier-us-east-1-ss-03). Observed behavior: Requests that orchestrate 2+ adapter calls show an additional ~80-250ms per adapter for synchronous schema/metadata lookups in the adapter-proxy path; some requests exceed client timeout (120s) or hit internal 30s gateway timeouts. Expected behavior: Adapter metadata/schema checks should be cached or performed asynchronously so per-request added latency is minimal (single-digit ms) and not compounded across chained adapters.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using customer's integration, send a multi-stage orchestration request that triggers adapter A (external data fetch) then adapter B (post-processing). 2) Ensure streaming responses are enabled and payloads include large prompt context (~8k tokens). 3) Observe end-to-end timing and any gateway timeouts. 4) Compare request traces with and without adapter chaining (single adapter).

investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage: Support reproduced elevated p95 latencies for multi-adapter flows in customer's dedicated pool. Single adapter flows show nominal latency.

03/10 - SRE traced pattern to adapter-proxy layer making synchronous metadata/schema validation calls to adapter endpoints prior to execution — validation was not cached for adapters flagged as ephemeral.

03/11 - Engineering hypothesis: recent change in adapter-proxy (PR 312) added an eager schema negotiation step to prevent mis-typed payloads; combined with cold adapter endpoints this yields additional network hops per adapter call.
03/11 - Observed that streaming + large prompt contexts amplify time spent in adapter handshakes due to blocking validation I/O on the request path.
03/12 - Verified that enabling a short-lived adapter metadata cache reduces added latency from ~95ms to ~8-12ms per adapter in staging.
03/12 - No indications of noisy neighbors or GPU contention in dedicated pool; serving-runtime timings are normal when adapter-proxy is bypassed.
03/12 - Risk: naive caching could mask schema drift; need TTL and cache invalidation on adapter deploy events.
comments: Aisha Patel [Support, 2026-03-10]: Customer reported ~15% of requests with 504s during peak (window 18:30-19:15 UTC). Attached traces and cURL reproducer.
ScaleSky Labs (customer) [2026-03-10]: We can reproduce reliably by chaining our 'lookup' then 'enrich' adapters; sending reproducer to support@redwood.
Miguel Torres [SRE, 2026-03-11]: Reproduced in staging. Confirmed adapter-proxy performs sync introspect call (schema negotiation) per adapter invocation. Opening INT ticket to track runtime change.
Lina Cho [Eng, 2026-03-11]: PR 312 introduced an explicit sync validation to avoid silent failures; propose moving to async validation + optimistic execution with background verification.

Miguel Torres [SRE, 2026-03-12]: Deployed metadata caching patch to staging (TTL=5m). Reduced per-adapter added latency to ~10ms in tests. Planning limited prod rollout tonight during low-traffic window.
Aisha Patel [Support, 2026-03-12]: Notified customer of planned workaround and requested confirmation window for production rollout.
workaround: 1) Increase client-side timeout to 180s and gateway timeout for affected routes to 90s (temporary). 2) For immediate mitigation, ask customer to reduce adapter chaining depth (combine logic into a single adapter) or use batched adapter calls. 3) For dedicated customers: enable 'adapter-metadata-cache' feature flag on their pool to short-circuit repeated schema checks.
resolution: Hotfix released: adapter-proxy v1.8.4 introduces short-lived metadata caching with TTL=5m, and a configuration flag to opt into optimistic execution (perform schema validation async post-invoke). Staged rollout: deployed to staging 2026-03-12; canary to 10% of prod traffic 2026-03-12 23:00 UTC; full prod rollout after 6h verification if no regressions. Post-deploy verification showed p95 e2e latency for multi-adapter flows dropped from ~1.9s to ~1.2s and timeout rate fell to <0.1% for the customer's traffic pattern.
next_steps: 1) Merge follow-up PR to add cache invalidation hooks on adapter deploys and webhooks from adapter registry (INT-8821). 2) Add integration test for multi-adapter streaming flows to catch regressions (tracking in ENG backlog). 3) Monitor customer-specific telemetry for 72h and schedule a post-incident review with ScaleSky Labs. 4) Update adapter runbook with guidance on feature flag usage and rollout checklist.
notes_for_cs: Customer-facing summary prepared for outreach: explain root cause (eager sync schema negotiation), mitigation (metadata caching + opt-in optimistic execution), and timeline. Offer to coordinate a config change during low-traffic window and provide log access for 72h monitoring.
